newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian economic team goes to Iraq for trade talks.
newsitem.headline: Syrian economic team goes to Iraq for trade talks.

text.p: A Syrian economic team left for Baghdad on Monday in the first such visit to explore the possibility of exporting Syrian goods to Iraq in line with the oil-for-food agreement between Iraq and the United Nations, officials said.

They said the team, led by Rateb al-Shallah, head of Syria's Chamber of Commerce and Industry, left through the Syrian-Iraqi border point in northeast Syria, closed since the early 1980s when both states severed diplomatic ties.
But the officials stressed the visit was an economic one and did not have any political meaning.
"The visit is purely economic and the team will hold talks with Iraqi officials and businessmen on how to conclude commercial deals," one official said.
He said Syria was encouraged to send the team after many world countries including some Gulf Arab states started to talk with Baghdad to get a share of the oil-for-food deal.
Syrian trade sources said the team, grouping leading businessmen, would offer to supply the Iraqi market with various Syrian food, medical and industrial goods which are manufactured locally.
"We have competitive prices for the goods we will offer and the close distance between the two countries will mean cheap transportation as well," one businessman accompanying the team said.
According to a deal with the United Nations Iraq will sell $2 billion worth of oil in six months to import its basic needs. Implementation of the accord began in December.
Syria has been abiding by the economic sanctions which were imposed against Iraq because of its invasion and six-month occupation of Kuwait in 1990.
Syria's ties with Baghdad deteriorated in 1980 when Damascus rejected Iraq's war with Iran and sided with Tehran throughout the war which ended in 1988.
Ties worsened in 1990 when Syria joined a U.S.-led multinational force which drove Iraqi troops from Kuwait in 1991.

But despite that senior Syrian and Iraqi officials visited the each other's capitals during recent years to hold talks on the sharing of River Euphrates waters with Turkey and the construction of a regional electricity network grouping Syria, Jordan, Egypt, Iraq and Turkey.
